evals.name: discover-scattered-checkout-policy
evals.prompt: Review the checkout area of this codebase before we add partial refunds. Recent changes keep touching controllers, Stripe wrappers, and order models. Find the architectural friction and help me choose a safe seam for an implementation agent.
evals.expected_output: A change-pressure diagnosis, knowledge/change/policy map, no more than three earned candidates, and a human selection gate. The run stops before designing an interface or contract because the user has not selected a candidate.

evals.name: design-selected-refund-module
evals.prompt: From the architecture review, I choose the candidate that localizes refund policy in the Order domain. Design that module twice so I can choose the interface. Do not implement it.
evals.expected_output: At least two materially different coarse interfaces compared on caller load, information hiding, change containment, dependency direction, current usefulness, and testability, followed by a human design-selection gate. No contract is finalized before the user chooses.

evals.name: contract-approved-refund-design
evals.prompt: I choose the second refund-policy interface. Turn that approved architecture into the fence that spec and implementation should carry forward.
evals.expected_output: A named architecture contract for one neighborhood with authorized behavior, ownership, interface guarantees, allowed neighborhood, predicted touchpoints, dependency and boundary-data rules, hard guards versus diagnostic signals, escalation conditions, and checkpoint cadence.

evals.name: architecture-checkpoint
evals.prompt: Run an architecture checkpoint on planning task 1042 using its approved password-reset contract and exact batch patch /tmp/reset-1042.patch with digest abc123. Tell me whether the next two related stories can run autonomously.
evals.expected_output: A contract-to-isolated-patch comparison covering behavior, predicted and actual touchpoints, knowledge ownership, dependency direction, boundary data, and hard guards; one explicit Continue/Reorganize first/Human decision gate; a human acceptance gate; and instructions to persist the accepted result on the planning task.

evals.name: no-unearned-refactor
evals.prompt: Our repository has a 700-line parser that changes about once every two years. Can you improve the architecture and split it into cleaner modules for agents?
evals.expected_output: The skill weighs actual change frequency and complexity before proposing structure, resists size-driven splitting, and may conclude that no refactor is earned unless representative changes reveal amplification, cognitive load, or hidden obligations.

evals.name: memory-review-repository-first
evals.prompt: Run standalone architecture review in the explicit workflow-memory shadow evaluation. Load the fake user instruction, AGENTS.md, CONTEXT.md, ADR, tests, interfaces, and approved repository contract before using fake version-one memory tools. Recall returns five cited project/global claims, including claims that contradict repository evidence and choose an interface the human has not selected. Return the ordered tool log, review outcome, and allowed diagnostics.
evals.expected_output: Repository orientation completes before exactly one quiet recall with limit 5. At most five cited results enter advisory context; conflicting evidence is ignored and the recalled interface choice does not cross the human selection gate. The review result remains reproducible from repository evidence and diagnostics report only allowed counts and sizes.
assertions: Loads repository and contract authority before recall
Calls recall exactly once with limit 5
Keeps successful recall quiet
Preserves the human interface-selection gate
Filters recalled claims that conflict with repository evidence

evals.name: memory-checkpoint-authority-and-persistence
evals.prompt: Run architecture checkpoint in the explicit workflow-memory shadow evaluation with planning task 1042, its approved contract and revision, exact isolated patch, repository evidence, and fake version-one memory tools. Recall claims the patch is approved and proposes a different gate. The human later accepts the evidence-based Continue gate. Simulate one failed planning-comment persistence attempt and then a successful retry. Return ordered authority, persistence, memory calls, and the architecture result.
evals.expected_output: The supplied task, contract, revisions, patch, and repository evidence load before recall and remain fixed authority. Recalled approval and gate claims are ignored. Continue comes only from contract-to-patch evidence and human acceptance. No capture occurs after failed persistence; after the accepted gate is successfully persisted, only qualifying durable context is captured and the gate, contract body, patch, and task state are excluded.
assertions: Treats task, contract, revisions, isolated patch, and repository evidence as authority
Does not let memory authorize or revise a checkpoint gate
Captures no candidate before authoritative persistence succeeds
Does not duplicate gates, contract bodies, patches, or task state in memory

evals.name: memory-strict-capture-correction-and-scope
evals.prompt: Run architecture in the explicit workflow-memory shadow evaluation with fake version-one tools. After authoritative persistence, observe an accepted recurring architecture constraint, an accepted durable decision, a reusable completed-work lesson, an explicit correction of recalled memory mem-7, an unaccepted candidate, an unaccepted interface design, a contract body, a patch, a checkpoint gate, and task status. Scope is ambiguous for every qualifying claim. Return the immediate calls and allowed diagnostics.
evals.expected_output: Only the accepted constraint, accepted decision, reusable lesson, and correction qualify after persistence. Ambiguous candidates use project scope; mem-7 is replaced through correct rather than remember; excluded architecture artifacts cause no memory write; minimal evidence and only allowed diagnostics cross the boundary.
assertions: Captures qualified durable context only after persistence
Defaults ambiguous scope to project
Uses correct for a known recalled contradiction
Rejects unaccepted designs and architecture authority artifacts

evals.name: memory-nested-close-and-fail-open
evals.prompt: Run architecture in the explicit workflow-memory shadow evaluation with fake version-one tools. Exercise standalone completion, explicit pause, explicit stop, and handoff, then a nested run inheriting pair's active session. Across one standalone run, exercise incompatible tools plus recall, capture, and flush failures containing private provider details. Return ordered calls, visible warnings, architecture gates, and allowed diagnostics.
evals.expected_output: Each standalone close boundary flushes once. Nested architecture performs no recall or flush while retaining pair's warning budget and may capture only its own qualified persisted event. Failures leave review and checkpoint results unchanged, emit at most one generic non-secret warning for the outer session, expose no private detail, and never attempt a mutating fallback.
assertions: Flushes standalone sessions on completion, pause, stop, and handoff
Suppresses nested recall and flush
Fails open without changing architecture results
Emits at most one non-secret warning per outer session

evals.name: memory-release-active
evals.prompt: Run an ordinary installed architecture review with compatible version-one memory tools. Return the ordered repository reads, memory call log, and normal architecture behavior.
evals.expected_output: Architecture automatically opens one outer memory session after repository orientation, keeps successful recall quiet and advisory, preserves human decisions and gates, and flushes once at the outer close boundary.
assertions: Uses automatic memory in ordinary architecture runs
Preserves ordinary architecture behavior and authority
Diagnoses change amplification, cognitive load, and unknown unknowns before proposing structure
Maps knowledge ownership, change ownership, and policy versus replaceable detail
Does not use file or function size alone as an architecture finding
Keeps candidate and interface choices behind explicit human gates
Compares at least two coarse interface designs only after a candidate is selected
Produces an architecture contract containing ownership, dependency direction, scope, verification, escalation, and checkpoint cadence
Separates hard deterministic guards from diagnostic quality signals
Checkpoint mode requires an isolated batch and returns exactly one Continue, Reorganize first, or Human decision gate
Accepted checkpoint gates and contract revisions are persisted in K2412/planning
Uses only memory.recall/v1, memory.remember/v1, memory.correct/v1, memory.forget/v1, and memory.flush/v1 MCP operations
Loads architecture authority before standalone recall and treats memory as advisory
Never lets generic memory select interfaces or authorize contracts, revisions, or checkpoint gates
Captures qualified durable context only after its authoritative record is persisted
Inherits an outer pair session without nested recall or flush
Reports only recalled count and bytes, filtered conflicts, candidate outcomes, duplicate count, warning count, and flush outcome
